key_insight: Localized diffusion-based optimization can generate hull variants that look promising under surrogate screening but still fail under high-fidelity CFD when viscous and pressure effects are fully resolved.
engineering_relevance: For ship designers, the work shows that physics-aware validation is essential before adopting generative hull changes, especially when optimizing only part of the hull such as the bulbous bow and forebody.
method: Parametric masking restricts diffusion-based edits to selected hull variables while preserving full-hull continuity.
A reward-directed sequential Monte Carlo sampler targets lower predicted calm-water resistance under displacement and stability constraints.
An automated viscous free-surface CFD pipeline compares generated hulls against a naval-architect-refined design and benchmark ships.
evidence_signal: Validated CFD on two benchmark container ships showed the generated variant matched resistance at Fn=0.195 but had 45-50% higher resistance at Fn=0.250 and 0.260, while GenHull E improved resistance only below Fn=0.240.
watch_item: Surrogate rewards that omit viscous pressure and stability terms can miss performance regressions, and the representation may not capture a faired bulbous bow adequately.
paper_title: Localized Generative Design of Ship Hulls with Diffusion Models and High-Fidelity Assessment
